headline_marked: Trial of [[former mayor Taposh and 27 others]] begins at ICT
headline: Trial of former mayor Taposh and 27 others begins at ICT
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal begins proceedings against former Dhaka South City Corporation mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh and others for crimes against humanity during the July uprising.
details: The trial of former Dhaka South City Corporation mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, former minister Jahangir Kabir Nanok, and 26 others has formally begun at the International Crimes Tribunal-1.
The accused are charged with crimes against humanity for the killing of nine people in Mohammadpur during the July uprising.
The first prosecution witness, Shahidul Islam Bhuiyan, gave an emotional testimony regarding the death of his son, Mohammad Farhanul Islam Bhuiyan, a Class XI student.
Shahidul alleged that police and Awami League activists attacked peaceful protesters near old Dhanmondi-27 on July 18, 2024, and opened indiscriminate fire, killing Farhan.
The witness further claimed that police and AL activists obstructed treatment for injured students at a hospital in Lalmatia and vandalized the convoy transporting the body to Rupganj.
In a separate case, witness Md Liton Mia testified against four accused, including former BGB officers, regarding the killing of 28 people in Rampura during the uprising.
Liton testified that police and BGB personnel opened fire on protesters near Rampura Bridge, killing several people, including 13-year-old Tamim Shikdar.
The testimony included allegations of helicopters firing tear gas shells and sound grenades over the protesters in Rampura.
caption:
Former mayor Taposh and 27 others face trial for crimes against humanity after the killing of nine people in Mohammadpur.

The trial of former Dhaka South City Corporation mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, former minister Jahangir Kabir Nanok, and 26 others has formally begun at the International Crimes Tribunal-1.

The accused are charged with crimes against humanity for the killing of nine people in Mohammadpur during the July uprising.

The first prosecution witness, Shahidul Islam Bhuiyan, gave an emotional testimony regarding the death of his son, Mohammad Farhanul Islam Bhuiyan, a Class XI student.

Shahidul alleged that police and Awami League activists attacked peaceful protesters near old Dhanmondi-27 on July 18, 2024, and opened indiscriminate fire, killing Farhan.

The witness further claimed that police and AL activists obstructed treatment for injured students at a hospital in Lalmatia and vandalized the convoy transporting the body to Rupganj.

In a separate case, witness Md Liton Mia testified against four accused, including former BGB officers, regarding the killing of 28 people in Rampura during the uprising.

Liton testified that police and BGB personnel opened fire on protesters near Rampura Bridge, killing several people, including 13-year-old Tamim Shikdar.

The testimony included allegations of helicopters firing tear gas shells and sound grenades over the protesters in Rampura.

headline: Lawyer loses eye after stone thrown at train in Brahmanbaria
summary: A lawyer was severely injured when unidentified persons threw stones at a moving train, causing him to lose his vision in one eye.
details: A lawyer was severely injured in Brahmanbaria when unidentified persons threw stones at a moving train.
The victim, who was traveling on the train, was struck by a stone, resulting in the severe loss of vision in one of his eyes.
The incident has sparked concerns over the safety of passengers traveling by rail in the region.
Local authorities have been notified of the attack, and efforts to seek the culprits responsible for the attack are ongoing.
